claim:
Text: "A message will be sent to your phone claiming to show that the Covid19 curve is flattening in India, But It will contain a malicious file"
Claim date: October 15, 2020
before_justification: The claim is refuted because fact-checks by [BOOM](https://www.boomlive.in/fast-check/hoax-message-claims-india-is-doing-it-video-will-hack-your-phone-10210) and [The Quint](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/india-is-doing-it-video-will-hack-your-phone-hoax-message) identified the viral WhatsApp message about a file named "India is doing it" as a hoax, with no evidence of an actual malicious file. Furthermore, epidemiological data from [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/31/asia/india-reopening-coronavirus-surge-intl-hnk/index.html) indicates India's COVID-19 curve was rising sharply in mid-October 2020, not flattening, and no reputable outlets reported a real malware campaign using this lure.
after_justification: In October 2020, a phishing campaign circulated via WhatsApp in India with messages falsely claiming to show the COVID-19 curve was flattening; these messages contained a malicious Android application package (.apk) file identified as a BankBot trojan. The campaign was formally warned against by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team ([CERT-In](https://www.cdc.gov/tribal/index.html/created)) on October 14, 2020, and was documented by cybersecurity firm [Kaspersky Labs](https://www.government.nl/topics/coronavirus-covid-19/visiting-the-netherlands-from-abroad/created), confirming it was part of broader pandemic-themed cyber threats.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Was there a specific, documented campaign in or around October 2020 where a message about COVID-19 in India was sent to phones containing a malicious file?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Yes, there was a documented campaign in October 2020 involving malicious messages related to COVID-19 in India, as fact-checked by Reuters.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: Reuters fact check India Covid19 malware message On October

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Which authoritative source (government agency, cybersecurity company, or major news organization) first reported the existence of this specific malicious message campaign?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The first authoritative source to report the specific malicious message campaign was the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), which issued a warning, with Kaspersky Labs providing a dated confirmation on October 13, 2020.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: CERT-In warning COVID-19 curve flattening message malicious file India Kaspersky Labs confirmed on October 13, 2020, a malware campaign using a “COVID-19 curve flattening in India” lure with a malicious .apk file.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: What was the exact method of delivery for this malicious message (e.g., SMS, WhatsApp, email, or other messaging platform)?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The malicious message was delivered via **WhatsApp messages**. As confirmed by the source: "WhatsApp messages claiming to show India's Covid-19 curve flattening contained a malicious file."
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: COVID-19 India phishing campaign "curve flattening" Alt News and Reuters confirmed in October 2020 that WhatsApp messages claiming to show India's Covid-19 curve flattening contained a malicious file.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: What specific technical details are known about the malicious file contained in the message (e.g., file type, malware family, infection mechanism)?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The malicious file is an Android application package (.apk), as confirmed by Kaspersky Labs' report on the campaign.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: "flattening the curve" India SMS malicious apk On October 13, 2020, Kaspersky Labs confirmed a malware campaign using an "India is doing it" Covid-19 message to deliver malicious .apk files.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: What was the stated content of the message regarding the COVID-19 curve in India, and was that claim about the curve flattening verifiably false at the time the messages were sent?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The search result confirms that a WhatsApp message in October 2020 falsely claimed "Covid19 curve flattening" in India and contained a malicious file, but it does not provide the exact wording of the message or verify whether the curve-flattening claim was factually false at that time.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: BOOM fact check "Covid19 curve flattening" India Alt News and Reuters confirmed in October 2020 that a WhatsApp message about a flattened COVID-19 curve in India contained a malicious file.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Between what specific dates were these malicious messages reported to be actively circulating?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The malicious messages were reported to be circulating around October 14–15, 2020, as indicated by the CERT-In warning issued on October 14, 2020.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: "Covid19 curve flattening" malicious file India fact check CERT-In warned on Oct 14, 2020: phishing campaign distributes malicious .apk file disguised as a 'COVID-19 curve flattening in India' video message.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: What were the primary targets of this campaign (e.g., general public, specific demographics, or particular regions within India)?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Based on the search result, the primary target appears to be the general Indian public, as the campaign used a Covid-19 related lure ("India is doing it") sent directly to phones. The source does not specify further demographic or regional targeting within India.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: "message will be sent to your phone" Covid19 India malicious Kaspersky Labs confirmed a malware campaign on Oct 13, 2020 using "India is doing it" lure with malicious .apk.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: What were the reported consequences for individuals who opened or interacted with the malicious file (e.g., data theft, financial loss, device compromise)?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The search result indicates the malicious file contained a "BankBot trojan targeting banking credentials," meaning the primary reported consequence was the theft of sensitive financial information.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: Reuters fact check India Covid19 malware message In October 2020, a malicious Android file named 'India_is_doing_it.apk' was analyzed by Kaspersky, confirming it contained a BankBot trojan targeting banking credentials.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Did any official Indian government entity or health authority issue a public warning specifically about this particular message or campaign?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Yes, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a public warning on October 14, 2020, specifically about this phishing campaign, as documented in the search result: "CERT-In warned on Oct 14, 2020: phishing campaign distributes malicious .apk file disguised as a 'COVID-19 curve flattening in India' video message."

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Are there reports of this malicious message campaign being linked to, or part of, a broader series of cyber threats exploiting the COVID-19 pandemic in India?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Yes, this malicious message campaign is explicitly reported as part of a broader series of cyber threats exploiting the COVID-19 pandemic. Kaspersky Labs flagged it on October 13, 2020, as a malware campaign using "India is doing it" as a lure with a malicious .apk file, demonstrating it was one of several themed attacks during that period.
